about: Which session leads on a day with two or more, and what to trim when time is short. One home for this rule: coach/tools/session_rank.py reads it, writes rank, rank_why and rank_keep onto week.json day rows in coach.json (build_dashboard.py), and prints the same call for the morning check-in. The Today card lists a day's sessions in that order. Works for any person and goal mix: floors and focus come from the person's profile.json, then the block, then the defaults here. No study tests 'which session to keep on a short day' directly; the steps are inferred from dose studies (sources by coach/research/LIBRARY.md id).

steps.text: Health first: on a red or Stressed day the easiest session leads and nothing hard is kept.
A race or test leads: its date is fixed.
A key session leads over anything that is not a race or test.
Next, a session whose skip drops that kind below its weekly floor (or a lift inside a lift_rank key period).
steps.source: TR-16 (cardio holds on 2 sessions a week with intensity kept); TR-17 (strength floor 2 a week); TR-36

steps.text: Ties go to the person's focus divided by how many of that kind the week holds: the first sessions of a kind do the most work.
steps.source: TR-19 (diminishing returns per set); TR-21 (diminishing returns per minute)
TR-18, TR-28 (order on the day matters less than the gap)

trim: Short on time: the lead stays whole; every other session goes to its Min (fallback_minutes). A session protected by a floor, a key or a lift_rank key period is shortened, never skipped; anything else may be skipped. Easy minutes go first, then extra sets.
trim_source: TR-16, TR-07 (keep intensity, cut volume); TR-19 (first sets do most of the work); TR-36 (hold lifting volume in a deficit)

lift_rank_key.text: Inside a plan.json fuel period with lift_rank "key" (every deficit period), lifts count as a floor and their focus is multiplied by this factor.
